clip.alt: A cross-section of the Earth: crust, upper and lower mantle, outer and inner core, with the curving paths of P and S waves from one earthquake, some bouncing off the surface and some crossing the core as K waves.
clip.caption: Waves from one earthquake bend at each layer. S waves cannot cross the liquid outer core, and that shadow is how we know it is liquid.

credit.what: Diagram of earthquake wave paths through the Earth
credit.source: U.S. Geological Survey, The Interior of the Earth (E. C. Robertson, 1966), figure 2; redrawn as SVG by SEWilco, Wikimedia Commons
